root_idea.summary: The root centers on concealing or keeping something out of sight.
root_idea.development: From the act of hiding or concealing, the lexical development extends to hidden stores or unseen things, self-concealment, shelters, and related derived and idiomatic nouns.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested noun is presented under its normalized classical citation form.

senses.definition: A hidden, concealed, or unseen thing; a stored reserve.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression concerning what is hidden in the heavens and earth, it denotes whatever is concealed or unseen and can be brought forth, rather than being limited to one particular physical object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hide or conceal something; to keep, preserve, guard, or store it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same concealment branch includes the related intensive or collective application and the transitive use explicitly cross-referenced for derived forms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become hidden; to conceal oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the intransitive or reflexive concealment use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put something enigmatically to another person and ask them about it; to propose an enigma.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction involves presenting an obscure question or matter for the other person to solve.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In established expressions, the hidden thing of the sky is rain, and the hidden thing of the earth is plants or herbage; the word may also denote seed hidden in the earth or what is hidden in its mines.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are conventional referential extensions of the hidden or concealed thing sense.
A lexical noun used synonymously with بِنْتٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who alternately shows herself and hides herself, or who stays in her house or tent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a conventional description of a woman characterized by concealment or seclusion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tent or tentlike shelter, especially one made of wool, camel hair, or similar material.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can refer to a particular tent structure and is also applied more broadly to a tent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mark made with a hot iron on a concealed part of an excellent she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized technical use referring to a hidden bodily location on the animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An artifice or stratagem that ends in disappointment; a failed stratagem.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical form explained as equivalent in meaning to خَائِبٌ, with transposition of the consonants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large jar or storage vessel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also pronounced خَابِيَةٌ, with suppression of the hamza in frequent usage.
A figurative or assumed-tropical expression, literally referring to the daughter of the jar.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or chamber for hiding or concealing things; a secret place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place noun, with the plural مَخَابِئُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A girl kept concealed from view, behind a curtain, or within a house or tent; also, a girl not yet married.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term describes restricted visibility or residence and has a recorded application to an unmarried girl.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who conceals himself in order to observe someone without being noticed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The concealment is undertaken specifically to watch another person secretly.
